thread:
eli: quick summary from the A/B smoke run on the int8 candidate (v2026-int8-01). ran 50k reqs over prod-like traffic slice.
maria: nice, quick numbers?
sam: pls paste the slice that showed the blip — iirc legal-summaries was noisy last time.
eli: numbers — latency p50 down ~12ms (from 142 -> 130), p95 down ~40ms. cost per token estimate down ~9%.
eli: quality: avg helpfulness score -0.6% vs baseline, exact-match for extraction tasks -0.8%, but hallucination events (policy-flagged) up from 0.09 -> 0.42 per 1k on the "legal-summaries" slice.
ana: whoa that halluc spike is concerning even if it's rare overall.
maria: can we see the example cluster for the hallucinations? short dump pls.
eli: pasted examples into the eval dashboard link: https://redwood.internal/evals/2026-int8-01/cluster-45 — mainly missing citations and invented statutes in long-form summaries.
corey: was this slice weighted in the A/B? could be sampling variance.
eli: we split traffic evenly across user cohorts for the 1% pilot; cluster concentrated in the subset that hits long-context retrieval paths.
sam: ok so rollout safety gating thoughts: current canary policy auto-promotes if latency improves and quality deltas < 1% after 10k samples. That halluc jump violates an implicit safety target.
maria: propose explicit fail-fast rules: if hallucination rate increases >0.2 per 1k in any monitored slice OR any slice shows >1.0% drop in helpfulness, abort rollout and fallback to previous variant.
eli: drafted a policy snippet —

```
rollout_policy: {
  initial_traffic: 1,
  ramp_steps: [1, 5, 20],
  hold_at_each: 3600, // seconds
  quality_checks: [
    {metric: "helpfulness_delta", max_delta_pct: 1.0},
    {metric: "hallucinations_per_k", max_delta: 0.2, per_slice: true}
  ],
  auto_fallback: true
}
```

sam: looks good. I'd add a hysteresis window — only trigger fallback if violation persists across 2 consecutive windows to avoid noisy single-window aborts.
ana: agree. add a smoothed metric: exponential window with alpha=0.3.
eli: ok i'll update.
corey: operational question: do we want to shadow new quantized model for an extra 24h on retrieval-heavy slices before any promotion? it might catch these context-dependent hallucinations.
maria: yes, shadowing is cheap and will give better signal on tail cases.
eli: deploy-bot: canary for v2026-int8-01 started @ 1726604400 with 1% traffic (pilot cohort: retrieval-heavy + control slice)
deploy-bot: monitor links: https://ops.redwood/metrics/canary/1726604400
sam: set alert: if hallucinations_per_k on any slice >0.3 for 30m -> page #eng-ml and revert flag.
maria: also add a metric to track citation-confidence and source-presence for long-form tasks.
eli: i'll run a focused shadow run across the legal-summaries slice for 12h and return examples + aggregated metrics.
corey: if the shadow run confirms, next step is to try int8 with per-layer bias-correction (small tweak) or fall back to nf4-int4 for that slice.
ana: can we add a quick smoke eval locally with a 200-example prompt set that reproduces the halluc patterns? i can run that in ~30m.
eli: appreciate it. plan: 1) shadow 12h, 2) run local smoke 200-example suite, 3) if still high, hold promotion and try bias-correction variant. hold policy: no auto-promote beyond 5% until the legal-summaries slice passes the parity checks for 48h.
maria: awesome. keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
sam: thanks — logging this into the rollout ticket: https://redwood.internal/rollouts/TKT-4892
eli: will post the 12h snapshot by ~1726608200.
